title: CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents
event_hint: CodeGrep: a 14B retrieval agent trained with GRPO to issue parallel grep/glob/read calls, injected into a frozen OpenHands agent on SWE-Bench Verified, preserving resolve rate while cutting rounds 15% and tokens 19%.
problem: Modern LLM coding agents (Claude Code, OpenHands) spend most of their token budget finding the file to patch rather than patching it. On SWE-Bench Verified a 30B OpenHands agent averages 23 rounds and 631K tokens per resolved issue, dominated by grep, glob, and view_file calls in ambiguous exploration loops, often 20+ rounds in a wrong direction.
mechanism: CodeGrep is a 14B-parameter retriever built on Qwen3-14B-Instruct, trained end-to-end with GRPO to emit up to 8 concurrent grep/glob/read tool calls per turn over a Git-worktree environment and return candidate files. Its output is injected into a frozen downstream coding agent (only the retriever is trained). A reward-design study compares three iterations; the final v3 moves the efficiency signal from the reward layer to the advantage layer and drops an auxiliary line-range term. Supervision is mined via CATM from 67K open-source agent trajectories.

evidence.claim: On all 500 SWE-Bench Verified instances, injecting CodeGrep lifts resolve rate from 25.8% to 27.0% (+1.2 pp) while cutting resolved rounds 23.0 to 19.6 (-15%) and resolved tokens 631K to 514K (-19%).
evidence.baseline: No-retrieval OpenHands baseline (25.8% resolve, 23.0 rounds, 631K tokens)
evidence.condition: SWE-Bench Verified, 500 instances, frozen OpenHands + Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507

evidence.claim: Downstream utility follows a precision threshold across three retrievers: BM25 at file-precision 0.375 hurts the agent, Jina at 0.445 is neutral, and only CodeGrep at 0.677 crosses the threshold at which retrieval begins to buy efficiency.
evidence.condition: Three injected retrievers on the same agent stack
evidence.source_locator: Abstract (PDF Page 1); Section 5.1 / Table 2, PDF Page 6

evidence.claim: BM25 injection degrades the agent: resolve drops 0.6 pp and resolved tokens inflate 21% (631K to 763K); on the 94 instances both configs resolve, BM25 rollouts spend 6.6% more rounds and 38.6% more tokens.

Reward design matters: applying the efficiency signal at the advantage layer (v2/v3) holds KL-to-reference at 0.09/0.15, versus reward-layer multiplicative scaling (v1) drifting to ~0.31 by step 900, i.e. roughly tripling policy drift.

Training scale: 67,074 raw trajectories mined (CATM) yield 31,977 effective training samples (47.7% retention); end-to-end wall-clock is ~27 hours on a single 8xB200 node, early-stopped at step 897 of a planned 2000.

evaluation_context: SWE-Bench Verified (500 instances); downstream agent is OpenHands with Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 (temperature 0, 100-round max). Retriever is CodeGrep 14B on Qwen3-14B-Instruct, emitting up to 8 parallel tools/turn, max 4 turns (3 exploration + 1 answer), 32 max tool executions per rollout. Training on a single 8xB200 node with LoRA via ms-swift. Retriever quality measured by file-level F-beta and precision (Table 2): CodeGrep v3 F-beta mean 0.576, precision 0.677, F-beta>=0.8 on 43.0%, 2.3 turns. The 25.8% baseline reproduces the published 25.2 +/- 0.7%.
limitations: The resolve-rate lift is small (+1.2 pp). Only one downstream agent stack is evaluated (OpenHands); retriever effect on other agents (e.g. Cursor, Windsurf Cascade) may differ, and the dropped line-range term could benefit agents whose editor consumes line ranges. LoRA (not full fine-tune) is used, and the model is released as such. The reward-design conclusions are specific to this GRPO/CATM setting.
project_relevance: Directly relevant to reducing code-agent read/grep/glob overhead. It shows a specialized 14B retrieval agent can shorten exploration while preserving task success, and it gives a practical decision rule (a file-precision threshold around 0.45-0.67) for when injecting a retriever starts to buy efficiency versus hurts the agent. The advantage-layer efficiency signal is a concrete RL-design lesson for tool-using agents.
source_notes: Resolve/rounds/tokens figures and the precision-threshold characterization are from Tables 2-3 and Section 5.1 (PDF Pages 5-6).
KL-drift comparison (0.09 vs 0.31) is reported in the Contributions (PDF Page 2) and Figure 2 (PDF Page 6).
Training scale numbers are from Section 3.6 and Table 5 (PDF Pages 5 and 12).
